transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because people keep telling me I’m making too much of things, but I’m not. I know when I’m being watched. The hospital people, and some people from the agency, they’ve been watching our house and even my cleaning routes, like checking up on me to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

And I do take care of him, you know. I’ve always been a hard worker, I clean the way my mother taught me, corners and baseboards, not just the middle where people look. But lately it feels like everywhere I go, somebody is looking, like they’re keeping notes. That’s why I came in, because everyone acts like I’m imagining it, and I need someone to understand what’s actually happening.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?

Yes… I mean, sometimes. Not all the time. When the house is quiet, especially by the kitchen, I’ll hear a woman’s voice near the window, clear like she’s right there. She tells me to check the locks, or move his pills.

And I do check the locks anyway, because you can’t be too careful—my mother always said a house should be kept proper, doors, windows, everything in its place. But the voice, it’s not like a thought exactly. It sounds outside of me.
Have you had any major medical illness or head injury before these experiences started?

I don’t know… I mean, not that I can point to. I’ve had the usual aches from cleaning houses, you know, knees and back, carrying buckets and bending all day, but a major illness or hitting my head bad before all this? I don’t think so.

Unless you mean something like when you get worn down and tired—because people don’t count that, but it does something to you. My mother used to say you can scrub a floor until it shines and still nobody sees what it costs you. But no, I can’t think of a head injury or anything like that.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?

Yes… my sister says that sometimes. She says, “Slow down, I don’t know what you’re talking about.” But I am talking about the same thing, it’s just all connected.

Like when I try to explain about my husband’s heart pills, then I remember the church schedule because that’s when someone could come by, and then the numbers on my client list matter too, because the order of them—well, people act like I skipped something. They say they can’t follow me, but I know what I mean. It just comes out tangled, I guess.
For longer than one month, have you been having these experiences of being watched or hearing the woman’s voice?

Yes… longer than a month. It’s been, I’d say, around eleven months now with the woman’s voice, and that feeling like people are watching us.

It started kind of small, like you think maybe it’s just the neighbors or the curtains not sitting right—my mother was always fussy about curtains, said people could see in if you didn’t hang them proper—but no, it’s been nearly a year. Not every minute, but on and off for about eleven months.
Since these experiences began, have you been less able to manage your usual work or daily responsibilities?

Yes… I have. I don’t like saying that, because I used to be the one people called when a house was a mess and they needed it done right. But the agency, they took away my supervisory routes. They said clients were complaining, and some of the girls I worked with said they couldn’t count on me the same way anymore.

And at home it’s been worse too. My husband needs things kept in order, and I always kept the house running, you know—laundry, meals, appointments, all the little things nobody sees. But lately my husband and my pastor have had to step in more, because I’m not keeping up safely like I used to. It makes me feel ashamed, honestly.
Have you become much less interested in being with other people or doing things you used to care about?

I’m not sure how to answer that. I mean, I still care about people… it’s not like I stopped caring. Sometimes I don’t feel like being around a lot of chatter, but then again, some people talk over you and don’t listen anyway.

I don’t know if that’s “less interested” or just me being tired of explaining myself. What do you mean by things I used to care about?
Have you found that your emotions feel flatter than they used to—for example, that your face shows less expression or your feelings seem muted?

I don’t know… flatter, like my face? I haven’t really been looking at myself that way. My husband might say I look tired, but he says that when I don’t put my lipstick on too, and honestly lipstick never sits right after a long cleaning shift anyway.

I still feel things, I think. I get upset, I get embarrassed… sometimes I laugh if something’s actually funny. But muted? I’m not sure. Maybe I’m just worn down. What do you mean by “flatter,” like not crying, or just not showing it on my face?
Since this started, have people told you that you seem less expressive in your face or voice than before?

I don’t think anyone has said it exactly like that… “less expressive.” My husband will say, “What’s that look for?” even when I’m not trying to have any look, but he says things like that when he’s irritated too.

And my pastor, he’s more gentle, he’ll ask if I’m tired or if I need to sit a minute. But I don’t know if that means my face is different. My voice… I mean, after cleaning all day, anybody’s voice gets low, especially if you’ve been around bleach and dust. I had one client once who kept all these little glass birds on shelves, and dusting around them made me so nervous because if one broke—

Sorry. I guess I’m not sure. Nobody has really told me plainly that my face or voice is less expressive.
Have you found it much harder to get yourself started on everyday tasks, even when you want to do them?

I’m not really sure. Some days I do drag my feet, but then, doesn’t everybody? If I know the laundry needs doing or the dishes are sitting there, I’ll usually get to it… maybe not right away.

Getting started is funny, because once I’m moving I can keep going, especially with cleaning. At work you don’t really get to sit around wondering if you feel like it—the sink is dirty, the floor needs mopping, you do it. At home it’s different, because the little things pile up, and then I start thinking about which one to do first, and then the phone rings or I remember I need to check if we’re out of trash bags.

So… harder? Maybe sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s “much harder.” What kind of tasks do you mean?
During the times when you hear the woman’s voice or feel watched, have you also been feeling depressed most of the day?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the day. Sometimes I’m scared or worn out when that happens, and then the whole day feels kind of… heavy, I guess. But I don’t always stop and separate out, like, “Is this sadness, or is this nerves, or am I just tired?”

Like yesterday I was folding towels and I kept thinking I heard something, and then I remembered I had left a rag in the bucket, which is the worst because it gets that sour smell, and then I got upset with myself. So was I depressed? I don’t know. I know I don’t feel right during those times, but “depressed most of the day” is hard for me to say.
Have other people told you that your behavior seems strange or hard to understand?

Yes… my husband has said I’m acting “weird,” mostly when I’m going back through the rooms after I already cleaned them. Like I’ll line up the spray bottles under the sink, or the towels have to sit a certain way, and if a chair is angled wrong I’ll fix it and then come back and check it again.

At work too, sometimes I catch myself arranging things in little patterns—bottles, towels, chairs—and walking room to room again because it just feels wrong to leave it otherwise. People don’t always say it straight out, but I can tell they don’t understand it. And then I start thinking about how some people don’t even rinse the sink after toothpaste, which is—sorry, that’s not what you asked. So yes, I guess they have said it seems strange sometimes.
Do you ever feel as if someone else is putting thoughts into your mind?

Putting thoughts in… I don’t know if I’d say it like that. It’s more that I’ll get a feeling, or I’ll notice something, and then people act like I’m making it up.

The reason I’m here is because everyone keeps saying I’m imagining things, but I know the hospital people and some people from the agency have been watching our house and my cleaning routes. They want to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. And it’s not like I just decided that out of nowhere—there are little things, like timing, and who shows up, and what they seem to know.

So no, not exactly putting thoughts in my head. More like they’re watching, and then I can’t stop thinking about what they’re checking.
Did these problems begin suddenly, within a couple of weeks?

No, not really within a couple weeks. It’s been… longer than that. I’d say this whole change has been going on about a year and a couple months, since after my husband was in the hospital for his heart.

At first I thought it was just me trying to keep everything together after that, because when someone comes home from the hospital there’s all these papers and instructions and you’re looking at the floors and the bathroom and thinking everything has to be right. But it didn’t just pass in a week or two. It’s been more like… around a year and two months now.
Has a doctor told you that you have a neurological illness, such as dementia, Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, or a stroke?

I don’t think anyone has told me that, no. I mean, I’ve been to doctors for regular things, and they ask all these questions and put things in the chart, but I don’t remember anyone saying I had something like that.

My husband had all the serious hospital stuff, so sometimes I get mixed up about which doctor said what to who, because there were so many papers and appointments… but for me, no, not that I know of.
When you talk, do people often tell you that you jump from one topic to another in a way they can’t follow?

Yes… people do say that. Mostly when I’m trying to explain what’s been happening, because it all connects in my head, but when I say it out loud it comes out wrong.

Like I’ll start with my husband’s heart pills, because that’s where I notice things, and then I’m talking about the church schedule, and then the numbers on my client list, and my sister will say, “Wait, what are you talking about?” or “You’re jumping around.” But I’m not trying to confuse anybody. I’m trying to get all the pieces in the right order, and they don’t let me finish.
Before these experiences began, had you started using any new medication or drugs?

I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t think so, but then there are always little things—vitamins, something for a headache, whatever someone tells you is good at church or at the store. I try to be careful because after my husband’s hospital stay there were so many bottles around, and I was always checking labels and moving things so they wouldn’t get mixed up.

But for me, like a new drug or something I started right before all this… I can’t really say there was one. I don’t use street drugs, if that’s what you mean. Medications, I’d have to look at the bottles or the papers because I don’t want to say it wrong.
Have people noticed that you show much less emotion in your face or voice than you used to?

I don’t know… I mean, I haven’t really noticed my face, unless I’m looking in the mirror, and who really does that except when you’re fixing your hair or checking if you look tired before work.

People have told me I look tired or serious sometimes, but that could be anything. When you’re cleaning houses all day and then somebody wants to talk and talk, you don’t always have a big expression ready, you know? My sister might say, “Why are you looking like that?” but she says that about everybody.

So… I’m not sure if it’s less emotion, exactly. I don’t think anyone has said it that way to me.
Before these experiences started, were you diagnosed with any serious medical illness?

I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve had the usual things checked over the years, like when they take your blood pressure at those little clinic visits or when you go in because you’re tired and they want to run tests, but “serious illness”… nobody sat me down and said it like that to me.

Before all this started, I was mostly working and taking care of the house, and there was always someone else’s appointment or paperwork to worry about. I’d have to look back at the records if you need an exact answer, because I don’t want to mix things up. But as far as I remember, no, I wasn’t diagnosed with something serious right before it.
Have you been having problems with your memory?

My memory? I don’t know… I mean, I forget little things sometimes, like where I put my keys or if I already moved the laundry over, but I think everybody does that, especially when you’re tired and going from one house to another and people are asking you things.

Sometimes I’ll walk into a room and think, “Now what did I come in here for?” but then I remember when I go back, you know? My mother used to say that means you’re doing too many things at once. I haven’t really sat down and thought of it as a problem-problem. What kind of memory do you mean?

doctor.question: Did these problems begin suddenly, within a couple of weeks?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This whole change has been going on for about 1 year and 2 months, since after my husband's cardiac hospitalization.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the time course and onset of the problems, specifically whether they began suddenly within a couple of weeks, which is most directly covered by the overall duration profile.

patient.answer:
No, not really within a couple weeks. It’s been… longer than that. I’d say this whole change has been going on about a year and a couple months, since after my husband was in the hospital for his heart.

At first I thought it was just me trying to keep everything together after that, because when someone comes home from the hospital there’s all these papers and instructions and you’re looking at the floors and the bathroom and thinking everything has to be right. But it didn’t just pass in a week or two. It’s been more like… around a year and two months now.

inference.note: F23.3 ruled out because onset was not acute (not within 2 weeks) and symptoms have persisted about 11–14 months with functional decline. Ongoing hallucinations, persecutory delusions, some disorganized/tangled speech, and decline in work/home functioning keep F20.0 highest; F22 and F06.2 remain differential.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is evidence of a medical or neurological cause for the psychotic symptoms, which would distinguish an organic delusional/psychotic disorder from primary schizophrenia-spectrum disorders.
doctor.question: Has a doctor told you that you have a neurological illness, such as dementia, Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, or a stroke?

target_item.reason: The question asks about a prior neurological illness such as dementia, Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, or stroke, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think anyone has told me that, no. I mean, I’ve been to doctors for regular things, and they ask all these questions and put things in the chart, but I don’t remember anyone saying I had something like that.

My husband had all the serious hospital stuff, so sometimes I get mixed up about which doctor said what to who, because there were so many papers and appointments… but for me, no, not that I know of.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is evidence of disorganized speech/formal thought disorder, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder or psychotic disorder due to another medical condition.
doctor.question: When you talk, do people often tell you that you jump from one topic to another in a way they can’t follow?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: When I try to explain what is happening, the words run from my husband's heart pills to the church schedule to the numbers on my client list, and people say they can't follow me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient's speech jumps between topics in a way others cannot follow, which directly matches disorganized thinking or speech.

patient.answer:
Yes… people do say that. Mostly when I’m trying to explain what’s been happening, because it all connects in my head, but when I say it out loud it comes out wrong.

Like I’ll start with my husband’s heart pills, because that’s where I notice things, and then I’m talking about the church schedule, and then the numbers on my client list, and my sister will say, “Wait, what are you talking about?” or “You’re jumping around.” But I’m not trying to confuse anybody. I’m trying to get all the pieces in the right order, and they don’t let me finish.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a plausible substance/medication cause for the psychotic symptoms, to distinguish primary psychotic disorder from psychotic disorder due to another medical condition or substance-related causes.
doctor.question: Before these experiences began, had you started using any new medication or drugs?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether symptoms may have been caused by starting a new medication or drug, but the provided symptom profile does not include substance or medication use as an item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t think so, but then there are always little things—vitamins, something for a headache, whatever someone tells you is good at church or at the store. I try to be careful because after my husband’s hospital stay there were so many bottles around, and I was always checking labels and moving things so they wouldn’t get mixed up.

But for me, like a new drug or something I started right before all this… I can’t really say there was one. I don’t use street drugs, if that’s what you mean. Medications, I’d have to look at the bottles or the papers because I don’t want to say it wrong.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are prominent negative symptoms, which would support schizophrenia over delusional disorder or psychotic disorder due to another medical condition.
doctor.question: Have people noticed that you show much less emotion in your face or voice than you used to?

target_item.reason: The question is about reduced emotional expression or flat affect, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I mean, I haven’t really noticed my face, unless I’m looking in the mirror, and who really does that except when you’re fixing your hair or checking if you look tired before work.

People have told me I look tired or serious sometimes, but that could be anything. When you’re cleaning houses all day and then somebody wants to talk and talk, you don’t always have a big expression ready, you know? My sister might say, “Why are you looking like that?” but she says that about everybody.

So… I’m not sure if it’s less emotion, exactly. I don’t think anyone has said it that way to me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is an underlying general medical cause for the psychosis, especially a recent medical condition affecting the brain or body that would support organic delusional disorder (F06.2) over schizophrenia (F20.0) or delusional disorder (F22).
doctor.question: Before these experiences started, were you diagnosed with any serious medical illness?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a prior serious medical illness, but the symptom profile does not include any item about the patient's own medical illness history.

patient.answer:
I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve had the usual things checked over the years, like when they take your blood pressure at those little clinic visits or when you go in because you’re tired and they want to run tests, but “serious illness”… nobody sat me down and said it like that to me.

Before all this started, I was mostly working and taking care of the house, and there was always someone else’s appointment or paperwork to worry about. I’d have to look back at the records if you need an exact answer, because I don’t want to mix things up. But as far as I remember, no, I wasn’t diagnosed with something serious right before it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is evidence of a general medical cause for the psychosis, especially cognitive decline suggestive of dementia-related psychosis, to distinguish F06.2 from primary psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you been having problems with your memory?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about memory problems, but the provided symptom profile does not include memory impairment or cognitive symptoms as an item.

patient.answer:
My memory? I don’t know… I mean, I forget little things sometimes, like where I put my keys or if I already moved the laundry over, but I think everybody does that, especially when you’re tired and going from one house to another and people are asking you things.

Sometimes I’ll walk into a room and think, “Now what did I come in here for?” but then I remember when I go back, you know? My mother used to say that means you’re doing too many things at once. I haven’t really sat down and thought of it as a problem-problem. What kind of memory do you mean?

opening_question.intent: Find out the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms for well over 1 month, including persecutory delusions (being watched by hospital/agency staff) and auditory hallucinations (hearing a woman's voice outside herself), with disorganized speech/tangentiality repeatedly acknowledged by others and functional decline in work and home responsibilities. This pattern meets schizophrenia criteria, paranoid subtype in ICD-10 terminology, more strongly than persistent delusional disorder because prominent hallucinations and disorganization are present. An organic delusional/psychotic disorder is less supported because no neurological illness, head injury, or clear medical cause was identified.
